data.title: Viettel, Singtel start building submarine cable linking Vietnam, Singapore and Thailand
data.description:
HANOI — Vietnam's military-run telecoms group Viettel on Thursday (Nov 26) said it had started construction with Singapore Telecommunications, or Singtel, of a new submarine cable linking Vietnam, Thailand and Singapore.

The Vietnam-Thailand-Singapore cable will stretch about 2,500 km and have a design capacity of 600 terabits per second (Tbps), with a completion target of the fourth quarter of 2030, Viettel said in a statement

The Vietnam-Singapore section alone will have a capacity of 240 Tbps, about 2.5 times the combined capacity of Vietnam's currently operating international cable systems

Other partners in the project include Vietnam's VNPT and FPT Telecom and Thailand's AIS, it said

Japan's NEC Corp and Singapore-based ASEAN Cableship are the project's contractors

Viettel currently participates in five of Vietnam's eight international submarine cable systems and carries around 65 per cent of the country's international connectivity capacity, it said

The group aims to be involved in about 10 international cable systems by 2030, including routes designed and led by Vietnamese firms.

Source: Reuters

data.title: Condo resale prices reach an all-time high in October 2026 despite fewer transactions
data.description:
Singapore's condo resale market saw prices continue to climb in October 2026, reaching an all-time high, even as fewer units changed hands. 

An estimated 987 resale condos were transacted during the month, down 5.9 per cent from September and 9.1 per cent from a year earlier.

The slowdown may be partly linked to increased competition from new launches. 

Luqman Hakim, Chief Data and Analytics at 99.co, said that, "October's new launches gave buyers more options, which may partly explain the slowdown in resale transactions."

He also added that Thomson Reserve and Lucerne Grand attracted strong interest after a quieter period for launches. Despite the competition, resale prices continued to rise across all three regions.

Condo resale transactions fall in October

Resale volume was also 7.5 per cent below the five-year average for October, pointing to a quieter month for the secondary market.

By region, the Outside Central Region (OCR) accounted for the largest share of transactions at 51.3 per cent, followed by the Rest of Central Region (RCR) at 31.8 per cent and Core Central Region (CCR) at 16.9 per cent.

Sub-sale transactions, which refer to secondary sales completed before a project is finished, made up 2.6 per cent of total secondary-market transactions in October, down from 3.8 per cent in September.

Resale prices increase across all regions

Despite the decline in transaction volume, condo resale prices reached an all-time high in October. 

The overall SRX Condo Resale Price Index increased by 1.3 per cent month-on-month and 3.8 per cent year-on-year. 

This follows a 0.7 per cent month-on-month increase in September, when the overall resale price index rose 3.5 per cent year-on-year.

Prices rose across all three regions, with the CCR recording the strongest monthly increase at 3.6 per cent. 

The RCR followed with a 0.8 per cent increase, while prices in the OCR rose by 0.4 per cent.

The CCR also led in annual price growth, with resale prices rising 4.3 per cent compared with October 2025.

The continued price growth suggests that the softer transaction volume has not translated into lower resale prices. 

Luqman noted that the widening gap between average new-launch and resale prices per square foot has helped resale condos remain competitive.

While new developments may appeal to buyers seeking modern facilities and fresh leases, resale properties can offer larger living spaces within a given budget. They may also suit buyers who prefer a completed home that they can move into sooner.

Highest resale condo transaction reaches $16 million

Nassim Park Residences. Source: Google Maps.

The most expensive condo resale transaction in October 2026 was a unit at Nassim Park Residences, which sold for $16 million.

In the Rest of Central Region (RCR), the highest resale price was $5.78 million for a unit at Pebble Bay. 

Meanwhile, in the Outside Central Region (OCR), the highest transaction reached $5 million for a unit at Waterfront Waves.

Condo resale owners record higher median capital gains

The overall median capital gain for resale condos reached $420,000 in October 2026, up $25,000 from $395,000 in September.

District 10, which covers Tanglin, Holland and Bukit Timah, saw the highest median capital gain. 

Meanwhile, District 4, covering Sentosa and HarbourFront, had the lowest at $73,000.

The overall median capital gain for resale condos reached $420,000 in October 2026, an increase of $25,000 from $395,000 in September. 

District 28, which includes Seletar and Yio Chu Kang, had the highest median unlevered return at 59.8 per cent. 

District 4 recorded the lowest at 4.1 per cent.

These figures compare each unit's current transacted price and its previous transacted price. 

As such, they reflect the capital gains and returns of units that changed hands during the month, rather than what all condo owners can expect to earn from selling their properties.

Will resale activity pick up in November?

Luqman expects a quieter launch calendar in November to potentially redirect some buyer interest towards the resale market.

He added, "Completed condos could appeal to those who want to move in sooner, while buyers with more flexible timelines may prefer to wait for new launches expected in early 2027."

For resale sellers, this could create an opportunity to reach buyers looking for more space, competitive prices and homes that are ready for occupation. The coming months will show how these changing preferences shape resale market activity.

data.title: OCBC adds new 100-tonne gold vault in Singapore to boost bullion capacity
data.description:
Singapore's second-largest lender has expanded its physical gold capabilities with the addition of a dedicated gold vault in Singapore, complementing its existing Singapore-based vaulting arrangements.

In a note to the media on Thursday (Nov 26), the lender said that the new vault will strengthen its ability to support growing demand for physical gold trading and custody services.

According to OCBC, its dedicated gold vault has approximately 100 tonnes of vaulting capacity — the equivalent of about 8,000 large gold bars, each weighing 12.4kg.

This, the bank said, supports its physical gold business ambitions, which were launched for its institutional clients and clients of its private banking subsidiary, Bank of Singapore.

It added that gold is expected to remain an important asset for portfolio diversification and wealth preservation.

Pointing to growing demand for its services, especially from Bank of Singapore clients looking for secure, long-term custody arrangements, the bank said that the increased capacity will put the group in a "good position" to meet long-term demand.

Meanwhile, the new vault is also expected to strengthen OCBC's role as a bullion bank in the wider ecosystem.

OCBC is a founding clearing member of the over-the-counter gold clearing system that the Singapore Exchange will launch in 2027 to strengthen the nation's position as a leading gold trading and distribution hub for the Asia Pacific region.

In addition, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has launched its central bank gold vaulting service, providing foreign central banks, international financial institutions, and sovereign entities with a secure option to hold gold reserves in Singapore.

OCBC said that it will continue to explore extending physical gold and other physical gold-linked investment and hedging solutions to additional segments across its group.

Its head of global markets, Kenneth Lai, pointed out that the new vault will enhance the bank's ability to support growing demand with institutional-grade custody capabilities, while reinforcing its broader commitment to the wider gold ecosystem. 

"As Singapore continues to strengthen its position as a gold hub, we are well-placed to support clients through a full suite of physical gold trading, custody and investment solutions," he added.

data.title: Singapore's manufacturing output grows 6.1% year-on-year in October as electronics sees sustained AI demand
data.description:
Singapore's manufacturing output grew by 6.1 per cent year-on-year in October 2026, improving upon the 5 per cent growth in September, amid sustained artificial intelligence (AI)-related demand.

Excluding biomedical manufacturing, output in October increased by 12.1 per cent, bettering the 10.9 per cent growth in September, according to data from the Economic Development Board (EDB) released on Nov 26.

On a seasonally adjusted month-on-month basis, manufacturing output rose 7.1 per cent in October, while output excluding biomedical manufacturing increased by 7.3 per cent.

Growth in all clusters except transport engineering, biomedical manufacturing

EDB data also showed that all clusters recorded output growth on a year-on-year basis in October, except transport engineering and biomedical manufacturing.

Precision engineering grew from the 39.7 per cent in September to 54.1 per cent in October, led by higher production of semiconductor equipment in the machinery & systems segment.

The precision modules and components segment also recorded higher output of industrial rubber goods, precision metal components and dies, moulds, tools, jigs and fixtures, EDB pointed out.

Electronics grew 6.6 per cent, with all segments expanding amid sustained AI-related demand.

Meanwhile, chemicals reversed a year-on-year decline trend to register a preliminary growth of 4.4 per cent in October.

General manufacturing industries also grew 0.5 per cent on the back of higher production of milk powder and beverage products in the food, beverages and tobacco segment.

But its miscellaneous and printing segments recorded output declines, with the former reflecting lower production of structural metal products and furniture.

Transport engineering and biomedical manufacturing saw year-on-year declines of 5.3 per cent and 35.8 per cent respectively in October.

The former was weighed down by lower shipyard activities and weak production of oil and gas equipment in the marine and offshore engineering segment, even though land and aerospace segments expanded.

The decline in the biomedical manufacturing cluster was due to lower production of biologics and a change in mix of active pharmaceutical ingredients in the pharmaceuticals segment.

EDB will publish the next monthly manufacturing performance release on Dec 28.

data.title: Sinopec follows Shell in second round of petrol price cuts
data.description:
About two hours after Shell posted reductions to its petrol prices on Wednesday (Nov 25), PetroChina-owned Sinopec also dropped its petrol rates.

In a price board update posted at about 7pm, Sinopec mirrored Shell's earlier four-cent reduction across its 95-, 98-octane and premium petrol offerings, while also keeping its diesel price unchanged. 

As with Shell, this is also its second reduction since Sept 14, when fuel prices first rose again after over two months of unchanged prices.

Its last three-cent reduction across its petrol and diesel offerings was recorded on Nov 18. 

Following the latest round of price adjustments, the price of the more popular 95-octane petrol at major fuel companies now ranges from $3.56 at Shell, Sinopec and SPC to $3.60 at Caltex and Esso. 

SPC has not raised prices since Oct 16, electing not to join the round of price hikes recorded between Oct 29 and Nov 2.

Meanwhile, Union Gas-owned Cnergy and Smart Energy are offering the petrol grade at $2.74 and $2.62 respectively.

Fuel prices fall in Malaysia

Across the Causeway, the Malaysia finance ministry on Wednesday evening announced a fourth consecutive week of reductions to its unsubsidised petrol and diesel rates.

The ministry said prices of its unsubsidised Ron95, Ron97 and diesel will fall by 25 sen per litre for the week of Nov 26 to Dec 2.

Following the adjustment, the price of unsubsidised diesel, Ron97 and Ron95 now stands at RM4.47 (S$1.40), RM3.75 and RM3.47 respectively.

It cited moderating prices of refined petroleum products, including for petrol and diesel, in the regional market during the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period.

Prospect of market surplus offset disruption concerns

Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday as the prospect of a market surplus offset concerns about disruptions to oil exports in the Middle East.

Brent crude futures declined 44 cents, or 0.5 per cent, to $90.96 a barrel at 6.35pm (Singapore time).

US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 62 cents, or 0.8 per cent, to $81.43 a barrel. Both benchmarks gained more than 2 per cent on Tuesday.

“Investors are preoccupied with the thought of supply exceeding demand,” said Tamas Varga, an oil analyst at PVM, a brokerage.

A build-up in crude inventories is also contributing to the softer oil prices, Varga said.

US crude stocks rose by 126,000 barrels in the week ended Nov 20, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.

Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude inventories rose by about 1.5 million barrels on average.

data.title: World stocks tumble as Trump tariffs rattle markets, AI rally fades
data.description:
NEW YORK/LONDON - Global markets retreated on Wednesday (Nov 25) with riskier assets under pressure after the Trump administration proposed sweeping new tariffs on 14 trading partners.

US stocks, hammered in the morning, partially recovered in the afternoon from early losses as investors bought the dip ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. The Dow closed higher and the Nasdaq and S&P 500 ended slightly lower.

US technology shares led declines amid concerns about inflation and a hawkish Federal Reserve, while investors assessed the implications of the tariffs for global supply chains and economic growth. Treasury prices rose as investors sought safe-haven assets.

MSCI's global stocks index fell 0.60 per cent and Nvidia shed more than 8 per cent during the day before closing down 3.91 per cent.

Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at Wealthspire Advisors, said bargain hunters were stepping in ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, adding that "investors are taking advantage of some of those discrepancies."

The Nasdaq was down more than 4 per cent earlier in the session before closing down 0.62 per cent, with the S&P 500 falling 0.25 per cent and the Dow up 0.33 per cent.

The selloff was mirrored elsewhere, with Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan down 1.99 per cent and emerging market stocks falling 2.8 per cent.

"We still have not dealt with the fresh shock of Nvidia and tech and now we have tariffs," said Aneeka Gupta, an equity strategist at WisdomTree.

"Markets are contending with AI, central banks remain hawkish, and then if we get a renewal of tariffs that adds volatility in markets."

European shares, which had traded higher earlier on gains in personal and household goods and retail stocks, later reversed course. The pan-European STOXX 600 fell 1.06 per cent.

Earlier in the day, the broad selloff, combined with lower bond yields, signaled growing concern that escalating trade barriers could weigh on global growth and corporate earnings. By the close of the US stock market, copper and aluminium prices had risen, and bitcoin had gained 0.81 per cent.

US Treasury yields declined on Wednesday but were off their earlier lows. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note fell 6.2 basis points to 4.84 per cent and was on pace for its seventh daily drop in the past eight sessions.

Nvidia gave up part of its gains from earlier this week, leaving the stock down about 10 per cent since Monday, when CEO Jensen Huang's return sparked a 31.5 per cent rally. S&P Global Ratings put the company at risk of a rating downgrade.

Data showed US consumer confidence increased by more than expected in November to its highest level in nearly two years. Separately, data showed the US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, and inflation increased further in October.

Rate expectations

The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of major peers including the yen and euro, fell 0.14 per cent, while the euro was up 0.11 per cent to $1.09.

The inflation and growth data reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027.

Euro zone government bond yields fell as the slide in US equities drove investors towards the relative safety of sovereign debt. Germany's benchmark 10-year Bund yield fell 4.73 basis points to 3.218 per cent, from 3.266 per cent late on Tuesday.

Brent crude futures LCOc1 settled $3.21, or 3.5 per cent, higher at $94.61 a barrel, after Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked ​Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery. [O/R]

Trading volume was low, and US markets will be closed Thursday.

data.title: Oil edges down as supply glut prospect offsets Middle East disruption fears
data.description:
LONDON - Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday (Nov 25) as the prospect of a market surplus offset concerns about disruptions to oil exports in the Middle East.

Brent crude futures declined 44 cents, or 0.5 per cent, to US$90.96 (S$118) a barrel at 1035 GMT (6.35pm SGT). US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 62 cents, or 0.8 per cent, to $81.43 a barrel. Both benchmarks gained more than 2 per cent on Tuesday.

"Investors are preoccupied with the thought of supply exceeding demand," said Tamas Varga, an oil analyst at PVM, a brokerage.

On Wednesday, Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked ​Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery ‌and Riyadh's financial district. Ras Tanura, Saudi ​Arabia's largest refinery, is part ​of a complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast ‌that ⁠also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude.

A build-up in crude inventories is also contributing to the softer oil prices, Varga said.

US crude stocks rose by 126,000 barrels in the week ended Nov 20, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.

Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude inventories rose by about 1.5 million barrels on average.

"Uncertainty about OPEC's 2027 policies in the upcoming Nov 29 meeting, especially with the UAE no longer restricted by OPEC+ policies and Iraq seeking higher oil output capacity, as well as broader market risk-off are some reasons," said Zhenqiang Seto, a senior research specialist for oil at LSEG.

OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on Nov 29 to decide on their 2027 output policy.

"Since the release of an IEA report this month, perceptions of a global supply glut have kept prices in check," said Tsuyoshi Ueno, senior economist at NLI Research Institute. Attention is also focused on how next year's production quotas will be determined at the OPEC+ meeting, Ueno said.

Iraq is pressing OPEC+ to lift its estimate of the country's crude oil production capacity, four people familiar with the matter said, heightening tensions over a review that will help determine how much members can pump next year.

Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has also reopened after an "unlawful group" closed a valve on the pipeline, with oil beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya.

"However, attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz and exchanges of attacks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have raised uncertainty over the sustainability of this trend," Ueno said.

A container ship was targeted and came to a stop on Tuesday while sailing an "unauthorised" route near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, according to state media.

On Monday, three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles as they sailed east through the strait, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Tuesday.

Source: Reuters

data.title: China Southern orders 50 jets in Boeing's biggest China deal in nearly a decade
data.description:
HONG KONG/WASHINGTON - China Southern Airlines said its subsidiary Xiamen Airlines agreed on Tuesday (Nov 24) to buy 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 planes at a list price of about $7.4 billion (S$9.6 billion), the largest Chinese airplane deal for the US planemaker in nearly a decade.

The order follows a commitment for 200 jets that China made during a summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing in May.

Jefferies said in a research note that it understood the planes, to be delivered from 2031 to 2034, represented the first conversion of China's 200-jet commitment to a firm order.

The US planemaker had been largely shut out of new orders from the world's second-largest aviation market since 2017 amid trade tensions between Beijing and Washington, though it has still been delivering planes from older orders.

Boeing and Airbus forecast China will require around 9,000 new jets by 2045 to meet demand, more than any other region.

China has not announced any specific orders as part of the 200-airplane commitment, and a China Southern securities filing did not say whether this order was included. Boeing, whose shares rose one per cent on Tuesday, declined to comment.

Airlines typically receive a large discount on the list price from manufacturers.

Trump expects more orders 

Trump said on Monday that he thinks China will buy another 250 Boeing airplanes. He gave no details, and Chinese officials have not confirmed any further purchases.

In May, he predicted China could boost its order to as many as 750 planes.

The 737 MAX jets in the Xiamen agreement are scheduled for delivery in batches between 2031 and 2034, China Southern said in the filing, adding that the deal is subject to approval from the company's shareholders and relevant Chinese government authorities.

China Southern said the order would help Xiamen Airlines seize opportunities arising from its move to the new Xiamen Xiang'an International Airport, support the construction of an aviation hub in Fujian province and optimise its fleet structure.

Xiamen Airlines, historically an all-Boeing operator, ended a nearly four-decade-long all-Boeing fleet in early 2023 when it took delivery of its first Airbus A321neo under an operating lease.

In April, China Southern and Xiamen Airlines also agreed to buy 137 Airbus A320neo family aircraft.

Source: Reuters

data.title: AirAsia halves Q3 losses to $119m as higher fares cushion fuel costs
data.description:
AirAsia Group narrowed its third-quarter net loss by 54 per cent to RM381.3 million ($119m) as higher ticket prices and capacity reductions helped offset elevated jet fuel costs.

The loss for the three months ended Sept 30 was 54 per cent smaller than in the preceding quarter, while revenue stood at RM4.7 billion, down 11 per cent year-on-year.

In a statement today, the airline said average fares rose 23 per cent year-on-year to RM305, while revenue per available seat kilometre increased 20 per cent to 22.50 cent, despite a 26 per cent reduction in capacity.

Passenger load factors remained at 80 per cent, suggesting demand held up despite higher fares and a smaller network.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation rose 42 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM629.4 million, supported by a 13 per cent reduction in operating expenses.

Jet fuel prices stood at US$152 ($196) per barrel, against a peak of US$183 in the preceding quarter. AirAsia said it recovered approximately 75 per cent of additional fuel costs through higher fares, surcharges and cost controls.

The reported loss included RM141.9 million in foreign-exchange losses. The company said that excluding these, its net loss would have been RM239.4 million.

Chief executive Bo Lingam said: "Our third quarter performance suggests that the worst is behind us."

AirAsia plans to increase capacity selectively during the year-end holiday season while keeping unprofitable routes suspended. It expects fourth-quarter load factors to improve, although average fuel costs could rise further.

AirAsia said preserving operating cash flow remained its priority as it pursued additional funding and restructuring discussions with creditors ahead of 2027.

Source: Malay Mail
